## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Trump, Xi, and Putin convene in Shenzhen on November 19 for first-ever trilateral summit amid Ukraine and Taiwan crises

China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on November 16 that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin will hold an unprecedented joint meeting at APEC in Shenzhen on November 19. The White House and Moscow had already signaled the meeting would happen. Trump heads to Asia as the summit looms; nuclear arms talks, trade truce renewal (set to expire January 2027), and Ukraine settlement terms are all on the table, though officials disagree on priorities.

**Why it matters.** This summit reshapes the geopolitical triangle that most affects India's macro picture—US-China trade, Russia sanctions regimes, and Taiwan's status quo. For a quant practitioner, the meeting signals either a great-power détente reducing volatility or a collision over Ukraine that hardens China-US competition. India sits between: the US wants New Delhi aligned against Beijing, but India trades heavily with both and imports Russian crude. Any summit outcome on trade tariffs, Taiwan, or Ukraine will ripple through Indian markets (Sensex, rupee, tech sector), and energy prices will swing on how hard Trump negotiates over Nord Stream alternatives and Strait of Hormuz threats.

**Action.** Watch for Trump's tariff stance on Indian goods (the section 301 duty is currently 10 percent; a 100 percent Russia-trade tariff looms if waived). Read the CNBC and Outlook India coverage for the confirmed agenda. Track USD/INR and crude prices on November 19–20; watch HDFC Bank and IT stock futures for spillover.

*Sources: [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/trump-xi-putin-ukraine-nuclear-tariffs-russia-iran-.html) · [outlookindia.com](https://outlookindia.com/international/xi-trump-putin-november-19-shenzhen-apec-yalta-summit-global-order) · [timesandstar.co.uk](https://www.timesandstar.co.uk/news/national/26729167.trump-xi-putin-plan-unprecedented-joint-meeting-apec-white-house-says/)*

### China simulates attacks on Taiwanese cities, deploys 30 warplanes near island as Xi prepares for Trump summit

China's military conducted unannounced drills simulating strikes on Taiwan's urban centers in the 24 hours before the November 19 summit, Taiwan's Defense Ministry reported on November 16. The exercises included 30 military aircraft, 8 naval vessels, and 3 additional official ships encircling the island. A Taiwanese security official told Reuters the drill was designed to show force ahead of Xi's talks with Trump and Putin—a signal that Beijing will not lower its territorial demands even as the three powers negotiate global order.

**Why it matters.** For an India-based market participant, Taiwan's status determines semiconductor supply—TSMC's fabs feed global AI and chip demand, including India's growing semiconductor ambitions. A military miscalculation or hardened Chinese stance on unification before the summit raises the probability of a conflict that would crater Taiwan Strait shipping, spike semiconductor prices, and trigger a new Cold War dividend for defense stocks (but crater supply chains). India's IT and hardware firms depend on TSMC; a Taiwan crisis would force immediate hedging in commodities and diversified sourcing bets.

**Action.** Monitor Taipei's official statements on the drills for escalation language. Track Taiwan Stock Exchange (TAIEX) and TSMC's ADR for volatility. If the summit produces no Taiwan settlement, expect semiconductor volatility through December; set alerts on USD/TWD and offshore volatility indexes (VIX futures, Asian vol).

*Sources: [kyivpost.com](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/90067) · [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/trump-xi-putin-ukraine-nuclear-tariffs-russia-iran-.html) · [cfr.org](https://www.cfr.org/global-conflict-tracker/conflict/confrontation-over-taiwan)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber now live for authorized penetration testers with 48.5% ExploitGym score.

OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber on November 5, 2026, a vulnerability-focused specialization of GPT-6 Astra, restricted to Daybreak Red authorized users. The model demonstrates 48.5% score on ExploitGym, up 51% from the prior GPT-5.6 Cyber's 32.1%, and achieves 40.3% recall on vulnerability discovery versus 32.0% for GPT-6 Astra. Phased rollout to all Daybreak Red customers is planned for the coming weeks.

**Why it matters.** This represents a measurable step forward in LLM-powered exploit generation. For security teams building automated vulnerability detection, the recall and ExploitGym metrics suggest GPT-6 Cyber will catch classes of vulns that GPT-5.6 missed. Defenders integrating this into their red-team infrastructure will need to rethink coverage assumptions on tools like SAST and dependency scanning. The fact that OpenAI gates this behind Daybreak Red with per-request monitoring, credential protections, and IP allowlisting suggests the security community is settling on the pattern that frontier models with critical exploit capability require supervised deployment—a constraint on how you operationalize this tooling.

**Action.** If you're doing security tooling on Azure or via OpenAI API, benchmark GPT-6 Cyber against your existing OWASP Top 10 test cases once you have Daybreak Red access. Compare the 40.3% recall and 48.5% ExploitGym against SAST baseline numbers from your stack. Expect you'll need to retune false-positive thresholds.

*Sources: [[https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber/]]([https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber/]) · [[https://thenewstack.io/openai-gpt6-cyber-exploits/]]([https://thenewstack.io/openai-gpt6-cyber-exploits/]) · [[https://tech-insider.org/openai-gpt-6-cyber-daybreak-red-exploitgym-48-5-percent-2026/]]([https://tech-insider.org/openai-gpt-6-cyber-daybreak-red-exploitgym-48-5-percent-2026/])*

### Anthropic cuts Claude Fable 5.2 price 20% and ships 30% faster output, with safety refusals down 55%.

Claude Fable 5.2 launched November 9, 2026, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens—a 20% reduction from Fable 5.1's $10/$50. Output generation is up to 30% faster. Safety blocks, the refusals that reject edge-case requests, dropped 55% from the prior version. Context window holds at 1M tokens and max output at 128K.

**Why it matters.** For teams running Claude at scale—internal tooling, customer-facing agentic products, enterprise deployments—the per-token cut compounds across millions of requests. The speed bump matters more than the price in latency-sensitive paths: code generation, real-time tool use, agentic orchestration all felt friction from Fable 5.1's tail latencies. The 55% reduction in safety blocks suggests Anthropic tuned filtering on clearly-safe operations (summarization, code formatting) while preserving guardrails on the hard calls. This signals a shift from broad refusal to narrow refusal—test your edge cases against 5.2 before rolling out to avoid customer-facing "this should work" complaints.

**Action.** If you're on Fable 5.1 in production, run a cost/latency audit on your top 5 inference paths: (1) calculate real savings with actual token volumes and cache read patterns, (2) profile tail latency improvement in your inference queue, (3) test 10–20 edge cases that previously hit safety blocks to verify they now pass. Plan the migration in one pass rather than gradual rollout—version skew in multi-turn agentic loops is hard to debug.

*Sources: [[https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/09/anthropic-upgrades-claude-with-new-fable-5-2-model-details-here/]]([https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/09/anthropic-upgrades-claude-with-new-fable-5-2-model-details-here/]) · [[https://techenclave.com/news/items/anthropic-releases-claude-fable-5-2-at-lower-api-prices]]([https://techenclave.com/news/items/anthropic-releases-claude-fable-5-2-at-lower-api-prices]) · [[https://www.elser.ai/blog/claude-fable-5-2-released-full-breakdown-of-new-features-benchmarks-and-pricing/]]([https://www.elser.ai/blog/claude-fable-5-2-released-full-breakdown-of-new-features-benchmarks-and-pricing/])*

## 🇮🇳 India

### Meganet Technologies files for ₹740 crore IPO to scale AI infrastructure amid India's data centre boom

Mumbai-based AI infrastructure provider Meganet Technologies Global filed its draft prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI on November 16, 2026, planning to raise ₹740 crore ($78.62 million) through a mix of fresh equity and an offer for sale by existing shareholders. The company, which supplies high-performance computing servers and data centre infrastructure to clients including Yotta Data Services and Motilal Oswal Financial Services, has clocked a revenue-from-operations CAGR of 72.87% between FY24 and H1 FY27, powered by accelerating AI workload demand.

**Why it matters.** Meganet's IPO signals that Indian infrastructure plays are reaching public market scale—essential for anyone building AI products locally. As an engineer consulting on inference or fine-tuning workloads, you'll likely see this vendor in RFP conversations. The ₹740 crore raise underscores the bet that India's AI race will drive sustained demand for domestically-managed compute—a moat against overseas GPU scarcity and cloud lock-in. For founders hiring ops teams or scouting partnerships, Meganet's public backing means more capital for ecosystem players to reference architecture and cost benchmarks.

**Action.** File SEBI's DRHP document for revenue run-rate and capex plans once published on the exchange portal. Track whether the IPO pricing attracts retail or institutional flows—a signal of confidence in India's AI infrastructure thesis. Cross-reference Meganet's customer list (Yotta, Motilal Oswal) with your own GTM to understand who else is betting on domestic compute.

*Sources: [upstox.com](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/ipo/meganet-technologies-an-ai-infrastructure-provider-files-drhp-with-sebi-for-ipo/) · [newsbytesapp.com](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/meganet-technologies-files-7862-million-ipo-plans-rs740cr-raise-to-grow/tldr) · [1027wbow.com](https://1027wbow.com/2026/11/16/indian-ai-infra-provider-meganet-files-for-78-6-million-ipo/)*

### JohnAIC closes $1.9 million pre-seed to build on-premise AI server infrastructure for India's enterprises

Bengaluru-based JohnAIC announced a $1.9 million pre-seed funding round on November 17, 2026, led by Crane Venture Partners with participation from Neon Fund. The startup builds on-premise AI server infrastructure designed to give Indian enterprises local control over inference and training workloads, sidestepping cloud vendor dependencies and data residency friction.

**Why it matters.** JohnAIC taps a structural gap: Indian enterprises building AI products—especially in regulated sectors like fintech and healthcare—need inference capability that stays on-premise and meets data sovereignty rules. If you're building a consulting practice around model deployment or training enterprise LLMs, JohnAIC's raise signals validator interest in the on-premise stack. For founders in AI fintech or compliance-heavy domains, this is a signal that hardware-software integration for India-first deployment is fundable. The Crane/Neon backing also indicates that tier-1 VCs see enterprise on-premise as a sustainable IRR play, not a temporary arbitrage.

**Action.** Reach out to JohnAIC's founders to understand their hardware sourcing strategy (domestic assembly vs. imports) and reference customer verticals. Track whether they form partnerships with system integrators or cloud resellers—that channel choice will shape which go-to-market motions work for downstream AI builders. File their Series A plans if they disclose them.

*Sources: [business-standard.com](https://business-standard.com/amp/companies/start-ups/johnaic-pre-seed-funding-ai-servers-on-premise-infrastructure-126111700132_1.html)*

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### TATACHEM (NSE): Rallies on RBI's renewed listing directive to parent Tata Sons

Tata Chemicals surged through the morning session on November 17 after the RBI reaffirmed in writing that parent company Tata Sons must comply with listing rules for upper-layer non-banking financial companies. The stock traded to a day high of ₹650–668 intraday, representing gains near 8–10% from recent levels (Nov 16 close: ₹612.10). The 2.5% stake Tata Chemicals holds in Tata Sons is often valued at a premium to its own standalone market cap, making regulatory clarity on the parent's listing trajectory material for the subsidiary's valuation.

**Why it matters.** The RBI's regulatory stance removes ambiguity that has haunted Tata shares for months. Tata Sons is now the only unlisted upper-layer NBFC—a signal that listing is no longer discretionary but a regulatory expectation. For India-watchers, this underscores RBI's willingness to act through formal channels when non-compliance persists. The read-across affects the entire Tata ecosystem (Tata Motors, TCS, Tata Steel): any parent-company discount to those multiples tightens if Tata Sons moves toward the public markets. For tech workers tracking domestic markets, this resolves a key governance overhang on a ₹7.8 trillion conglomerate and validates the domestic regulator's credibility on enforcement.

**Action.** The RBI's October 1 letter to Tata Sons (available via RBI Financial System website press releases) and the formal November 17 follow-up establish the directive. Watch the Tata Trusts' next response—Noel Tata and the Tata Trusts control 66% and have opposed listing. The stock will re-rate if the trust signals acceptance. File to watch: Tata Sons' formal compliance communication to the RBI, expected within 60 days per upper-layer norms.

*Sources: [[RBI tells Tata Sons follow listing rules, Tata Chemicals jumps](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/rbi-tells-tata-sons-follow-listing-rules-tata-chemicals-jumps/tldr)]([RBI tells Tata Sons follow listing rules, Tata Chemicals jumps](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/rbi-tells-tata-sons-follow-listing-rules-tata-chemicals-jumps/tldr)) · [[Tata Sons listing: RBI makes its stand clear again, asks the company to comply](https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/tata-sons-listing-rbi-makes-its-stand-clear-again-asks-the-company-to-comply-567742-2026-11-17)]([Tata Sons listing: RBI makes its stand clear again, asks the company to comply](https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/tata-sons-listing-rbi-makes-its-stand-clear-again-asks-the-company-to-comply-567742-2026-11-17)) · [[Tata Investment Share Price Up 2.9% as RBI Presses Tata Sons Listing](https://businessupturn.com/finance/stock-market/tata-investment-corporation-shares-rise-2-9-to-rs593-after-rbi-tells-tata-sons-in-writing-to-comply-with-listing-rules/)]([Tata Investment Share Price Up 2.9% as RBI Presses Tata Sons Listing](https://businessupturn.com/finance/stock-market/tata-investment-corporation-shares-rise-2-9-to-rs593-after-rbi-tells-tata-sons-in-writing-to-comply-with-listing-rules/))*

### URBANCO (NSE): Opens ₹2,500 crore QIP as Urban Company signals growth spending intent

Urban Company launched a qualified institutional placement on November 17 at a floor price of ₹161.03 per share, targeting up to ₹2,500 crore in fresh capital. The stock closed at ₹171.60 on November 16 (up 1.72% that day), implying the QIP floor sits roughly 6% below the prior close—typical for institutions negotiating entry. The company has allocated ₹600 crore of the raise to build supply-side infrastructure for InstaHelp, its high-margin home-services vertical, with the remainder reserved for M&A, new ventures, and corporate needs.

**Why it matters.** Urban Company's Q2FY27 showed expanding losses (₹182.5 crore vs. ₹59.3 crore YoY), yet the capital market still backed a ₹2,500 crore raise with 99.3% shareholder approval—a signal that institutional investors believe the company's unit economics will improve as it scales supply. The InstaHelp bet reads as a push to capture India's fragmented home-services market before larger players invest. For the domestic startup-to-public pipeline, this validates investor appetite for loss-making platforms at scale; ₹2,500 crore is a material bet on operational leverage in a low-moat vertical.

**Action.** Shareholder approval arrived November 15; the QIP window opened November 17 and will close within the next two weeks (final issue price to be set with book runners). Monitor NSE announcements for allotment date and final offer price. Watch Q3FY27 earnings (expected late January 2027) for unit economics and cash-burn trajectory—the raise buys 18–24 months of runway at current burn. The floor price of ₹161.03 is your entry-level watch; placement success above ₹170 signals institutional conviction.

*Sources: [[Urban Company Opens INR 2,500 Cr QIP at INR 161.03 Floor Price](https://india.entrepreneur.com/business-news/urban-company-opens-inr-2500-cr-qip-at-inr-161-03-floor-price)]([Urban Company Opens INR 2,500 Cr QIP at INR 161.03 Floor Price](https://india.entrepreneur.com/business-news/urban-company-opens-inr-2500-cr-qip-at-inr-161-03-floor-price)) · [[Urban Company shares in focus as Rs 2,500 crore QIP under progress](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/urban-company-shares-in-focus-rs-2500-crore-qip-under-progress-567746-2026-11-17)]([Urban Company shares in focus as Rs 2,500 crore QIP under progress](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/urban-company-shares-in-focus-rs-2500-crore-qip-under-progress-567746-2026-11-17)) · [[Urban Company Opens Rs 2,500 Crore QIP, Sets Share Price at Rs 161.03](https://viestories.com/press-release/urban-company-opens-rs-2500-crore-qip-sets-share-price-at-rs-16103-12815967)]([Urban Company Opens Rs 2,500 Crore QIP, Sets Share Price at Rs 161.03](https://viestories.com/press-release/urban-company-opens-rs-2500-crore-qip-sets-share-price-at-rs-16103-12815967))*

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### DNA medicine startup Seawolf launches with $100M Series A, Sanofi partnership worth up to $1.2 billion

Seawolf Therapeutics, led by CEO Elizabeth Alcamo, emerged from stealth on November 16 with $100 million in combined seed and Series A funding. The San Diego-based company inked a multi-target DNA medicines research collaboration and exclusive license deal with Sanofi valued at up to $1.2 billion in milestone payments. Versant Ventures co-led both the seed and Series A rounds alongside MPM BioImpact and Novartis Venture Fund, with Eli Lilly and CRISPR Therapeutics participating.

**Why it matters.** Pharma validation for redosable DNA-based therapeutics is rare — Seawolf's TRIDENT lipid nanoparticle delivery platform cleared a major hurdle by securing a partnership with a tier-one player like Sanofi before entering human trials. This signals that DNA medicine platforms (distinct from CRISPR or mRNA) are maturing enough for large-scale commercial bets. Founders backing biotech are increasingly focused on modular delivery systems; Seawolf's LNP-based approach mirrors the playbook that made mRNA viable in 2015–2020. Expect to see more non-AI deeptech companies following this path: big pharma providing validation, VCs providing scale capital.

**Action.** Track Seawolf's clinical timeline — the company expects to pick a lead candidate by late 2027 and file IND by end of 2028. Read Sanofi's most recent investor letters for cues on how big pharma is rebalancing around alternative modalities. Find the Versant thesis docs on DNA medicines; they're a feeder source for which labs have the strongest LNP chemistry.

### Nordic VCs and founders back Stoa's €3.5M pre-seed for AI-driven construction management targeting data centre boom

Helsinki-based Stoa raised €3.5 million in pre-seed funding on November 16, led by Lifeline Ventures and backed by a constellation of Nordic founder-angels including Supercell co-founder Ilkka Paananen, Wolt co-founder Miki Kuusi, former Nokia CEO Pekka Lundmark, and PlanGrid co-founders Tracy Young and Ralph Gootee. Illusian and Wave Ventures also participated. The company serves 25-plus construction and data centre sites across the Nordics and is now expanding to the UK and US markets.

**Why it matters.** Construction tooling remains fragmented and neglected by enterprise software; Stoa's AI-driven system consolidating drawings, schedules, QA and safety reports is addressing a real gap as hyperscalers race to build data centre capacity across Europe and North America. The founder roster — exits from fintech (Wolt), gaming (Supercell), and infrastructure (PlanGrid, Nokia) — signals that Nordic VCs see construction as the next frontier for applied AI outside of core tech. Data centre expansion is a forcing function; managing thousands of concurrent tasks on a single site makes manual coordination a liability. This is the kind of boring-infrastructure play that rarely makes headlines but compounds returns quietly.

**Action.** Watch Stoa's expansion into US data centre markets — where they compete against Bridger & Palfinger and legacy CMMS vendors. CEO Johannes Korpela is the founder to track; his speed to close a pre-seed in under a week suggests strong founder-market fit or investor pull. Scan PlanGrid's post-acquisition playbook at Trimble for a comparable scaling arc.

*Sources: [[https://tech.eu/2026/11/16/backed-by-supercell-wolt-and-plangrid-founders-stoa-lands-eur35m-to-bring-ai-to-construction-sites](https://tech.eu/2026/11/16/backed-by-supercell-wolt-and-plangrid-founders-stoa-lands-eur35m-to-bring-ai-to-construction-sites)]([https://tech.eu/2026/11/16/backed-by-supercell-wolt-and-plangrid-founders-stoa-lands-eur35m-to-bring-ai-to-construction-sites](https://tech.eu/2026/11/16/backed-by-supercell-wolt-and-plangrid-founders-stoa-lands-eur35m-to-bring-ai-to-construction-sites)) · [[https://www.startup.eu/investments/stoa-3-5-m-pre-seed-11-2026](https://www.startup.eu/investments/stoa-3-5-m-pre-seed-11-2026)]([https://www.startup.eu/investments/stoa-3-5-m-pre-seed-11-2026](https://www.startup.eu/investments/stoa-3-5-m-pre-seed-11-2026)) · [[https://bricks-bytes.com/daily-blueprint/16-nov-2026/](https://bricks-bytes.com/daily-blueprint/16-nov-2026/)]([https://bricks-bytes.com/daily-blueprint/16-nov-2026/](https://bricks-bytes.com/daily-blueprint/16-nov-2026/))*

## 🩹 Health & Science

### Hidden Genetic Differences in Gut Bacteria Link to Metabolic Health and Aging

A Nature study identified 940 independent associations between genetic variants within gut bacteria species and human health traits, including metabolic markers. Researchers analyzed phenotype-wide associations and found that microbial genetic diversity—not just species presence—predicts blood pressure, BMI, cholesterol, triglycerides, bile acid metabolism, and blood cell counts. Critically, 65.74% of these associations showed no link to bacterial species abundance, meaning two people colonized with identical bacterial species can have very different metabolic signatures based on the microbes' genetic makeup.

**Why it matters.** This inverts the assumption that "healthy microbiome" means specific bacterial species. Instead, the genetic background of *strains within those species* drives metabolic outcome. For longevity researchers: a pathway to precision microbiome matching—selecting strains by genotype, not taxonomy. For AI-in-health builders: microbiome profiling and probiotic selection must incorporate variant data, creating new data moats and diagnostic opportunities.

**Action.** Locate the November 2026 Nature paper (the News-Medical coverage cited it but did not name the authors—pull from nature.com or PubMed). The 940-association map is immediately usable as a reference for microbiome-metabolic phenotype research. This finding justifies clinical trials testing strain-level microbiome matching rather than species-level swap-outs. It also flags probiotic vendors that only report genus/species without genetic profiling as outdated.

*Sources: [[Hidden genetic differences in gut bacteria may hold clues to aging](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261105/Hidden-genetic-differences-in-gut-bacteria-may-hold-clues-to-aging.aspx)]([Hidden genetic differences in gut bacteria may hold clues to aging](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261105/Hidden-genetic-differences-in-gut-bacteria-may-hold-clues-to-aging.aspx)) · [Nature (November 2026, full text via nature.com)](Nature (November 2026, full text via nature.com))*

## 🎤 Culture & World

### Radio City Rockettes Cap Centennial Year With Record-Breaking 230-Performance 2026 Christmas Spectacular Season

The Radio City Christmas Spectacular is in its second century with 230 performances running through January 4, 2027 — the most shows since the production debuted in 1933. The venue added new choreography including a tap piece called "Ring" set to "Carol of the Bells" that builds from three dancers to all 36 Rockettes for the finale. The 2025 centennial season drew the production's highest attendance in 25 years.

**Why it matters.** Live entertainment in physical venues continues to command cultural weight and audience loyalty despite streaming's dominance. The Rockettes represent one of the few remaining annual cultural tentpoles that drive New York attendance and holiday spend patterns, signaling where consumer culture still moves in-person.

**Action.** Watch whether the 230-show run achieves its attendance projection and what percentage of seats fill for weekday versus weekend performances. The on-stage camera innovation — overhead formation shots broadcast live during the show — is a subtle signal of how traditional theater is adopting digital-hybrid presentation models.

*Sources: [[ABC7 New York](https://abc7ny.com/post/radio-city-rockettes-mark-100-years-christmas-spectacular-new-york/18120118/)]([ABC7 New York](https://abc7ny.com/post/radio-city-rockettes-mark-100-years-christmas-spectacular-new-york/18120118/)) · [[Playbill](https://playbill.com/article/radio-city-christmas-spectacular-sets-2026-return-featuring-230-performances-starring-the-rockettes)]([Playbill](https://playbill.com/article/radio-city-christmas-spectacular-sets-2026-return-featuring-230-performances-starring-the-rockettes)) · [[TheaterMania](https://www.theatermania.com/news/rockettes-reveal-details-for-brand-new-christmas-spectacular-number_1854703/)]([TheaterMania](https://www.theatermania.com/news/rockettes-reveal-details-for-brand-new-christmas-spectacular-number_1854703/))*
